newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shares end sharply higher on shekel fall.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shares end sharply higher on shekel fall.

text.p: Israeli shares closed nearly two percent higher on Tuesday on sharply higher turnover following the decline of the shekel against the dollar, traders said.
The benchmark Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 1.96 percent, or 3.78 points, to 202.68 on all-share turnover of 101 million shekels against 68 million shekels on Monday.
The Maof 25 blue chip index gained 2.38 percent to 213.80.

"The market looks very good and investors are very optimistic," said Amitay Tafla at Sigma Securities. "Trading opened with mild decline but (prices) started rising following the strong decline of the shekel against the dollar."

"Activity rose sharply and the Maof index rose above 210 points, which is believed to be a strong barrier. The mood in the market is very positive and investors expect the positive trend will continue," Tafla said.

Other traders were less optimistic saying that the market would not recover before approval of the 1997 budget. Traders said they expected the Bank of Israel to cut its key lending rate following the parliamentary approval of the budget. Parliament has until December 31 to approve the package.
"The stock market was following the dollar's rise today and activity has improved. But it is still too early to talk about a real change in the market," said a trader at United Mizrahi Bank.
"The rise of the market today might also be an outcome of activity of portfolio mangers and mutual funds that want to show improved results before the end of the year," he said.

Koor Industries, the most active share gained 0.25 percent to 27,948 on a volume of 16.1 million shekels. Lehman Brothers said it was maintaining its 2-outperform rating for the share, saying it was trading at a discount of approximately 23 percent to underlying value.

Bezeq Israel Telecom, the second most active share, surged 6.75 percent to 823 on volume 9.1 million shekels. Traders said it was a technical correction after the share suffered heavy losses during the last few weeks.
Israel Chemicals rose 1.25 percent to 284 on volume 6.5 million shekels.
Osem Investments closed unchanged at 1,799. Salomon Brothers said the share would underperform the market due to a modest growth outlook and a relatively high share price valuation.
